headline: Underwriting gains and eased litigation costs lift profit
summary_short: CVS Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $106.1 billion, up 7.3% y/y, with net income attributable to CVS Health of $2.98 billion (+191.8% y/y) and diluted EPS of $2.31, as improved Health Care Benefits underwriting and the absence of $833 million in prior-year litigation charges drove the rebound.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.3% y/y to $106.1 billion on growth across all four segments, led by Health Services (+11.5% to $51.8 billion) on pharmacy drug mix, brand inflation, and Rite Aid volume. Operating income nearly doubled (+97.5% y/y, $4.7 billion), driven by improved Health Care Benefits underwriting -- MBR fell to 87.4% from 89.9% on stronger Government-business performance and the absence of a $471 million prior-year Medicare Advantage reserve -- plus the absence of $833 million in legacy litigation charges booked a year ago. Net income reached $2.98 billion ($2.31 diluted EPS). Cash fell to $11.3 billion from $11.8 billion y/y; equity rose to $79.7 billion. No forward guidance was disclosed in this 10-Q.
